lessons.title: Know the Main Hand Tool Families
lessons.objective: Recognize common hand tools and their purposes.
lessons.why_this_matters: A customer may describe a job without knowing the name of the tool.

content_sections.heading: Driving and turning
paragraphs: Screwdrivers turn screws. Wrenches and sockets turn matching nuts or bolt heads. Pliers grip, bend, or cut within their intended use.

content_sections.heading: Measuring and marking
paragraphs: Tape measures, squares, and levels help check dimensions, angles, and alignment. Marking tools help transfer measurements to a workpiece.

content_sections.heading: Cutting and striking
paragraphs: Hand saws cut suitable materials. Utility knives cut materials allowed by the blade and tool instructions. Hammers strike nails or other items when designed for that purpose.

lessons.hardware_store_example: A customer asks for a tool to tighten a hex nut under a sink. You show a correctly sized wrench and ask about clearance before recommending one.
what_to_say_or_do: Ask what the customer needs to do.
Show two suitable tool categories when helpful.
Explain each tool in everyday language.
common_mistakes: Recommending a tool from its appearance alone.
Using a cutting tool for a task it was not designed to perform.
lessons.when_to_ask_for_help: Ask for help with specialized tools, energized systems, and applications requiring professional qualifications.

lessons.title: Choose the Right Size and Fit
lessons.objective: Match tools to fasteners, materials, and working space.
lessons.why_this_matters: A correct tool type can still be wrong if it does not fit.

content_sections.heading: Fit first
paragraphs: Choose a screwdriver tip, socket, or wrench that matches the fastener type and size. Poor fit can round or strip parts.

content_sections.heading: Consider access
paragraphs: A deep socket, short handle, or different wrench shape may help in a tight area. Check the actual clearance before recommending a specific design.

content_sections.heading: Choose by job
paragraphs: A hand saw must be appropriate for the material. A measuring tool must offer the range and precision the customer needs. Verify tool specifications rather than assuming.

lessons.hardware_store_example: A customer needs to tighten a bolt behind a cabinet. You ask about the space around the bolt and the head size. You compare tool options without guaranteeing clearance.
what_to_say_or_do: Check packaging for material and tool limits.
common_mistakes: Using adjustable tools carelessly on a poorly matched head.
lessons.when_to_ask_for_help: Escalate if the customer cannot identify the fastener or if tool use could damage safety-critical equipment.

unscored_practice.answer: Confirm size and shape. Ask about working space.

lessons.title: Measure, Mark, and Check Work
lessons.objective: Explain basic measuring and layout tools.
lessons.why_this_matters: A small measuring mistake can waste materials or make parts fail to fit.

content_sections.heading: Measure carefully
paragraphs: Start at the correct reference point. Read the unit marks and record the number. Measure again before cutting.

content_sections.heading: Keep things straight
paragraphs: A level checks orientation against level or plumb. A square helps check or mark right angles. Use each tool according to its design.

content_sections.heading: Communicate measurements
paragraphs: Repeat the number and unit. A measurement of 24 inches is not the same as 24 centimeters. Ask whether the measurement is exact or approximate.

lessons.hardware_store_example: A customer wants a shelf cut to size. You ask whether their measurement includes brackets and have them confirm the unit and finished dimension.
what_to_say_or_do: Say the unit with every measurement.
Measure twice before an irreversible cut.
common_mistakes: Measuring from the wrong end of a damaged tape.
lessons.when_to_ask_for_help: Ask for help with precision layout, building-code questions, and store cutting services.

supporting_materials.purpose: Identify tool/fastener features and compare real products
supporting_materials.accessibility: Provide descriptive alt text naming the visible components. Do not use imagery as the only teaching source.

key_takeaways: Start at the correct reference point.

unscored_practice.question: Before recommending a product, what would you check in this situation? A customer wants a shelf cut to size. You ask whether their measurement includes brackets and have them confirm the unit and finished dimension.
unscored_practice.answer: Say the unit with every measurement. Check the reference edge.

lessons.title: Explain Basic Hand Tool Safety
lessons.objective: Recognize common risks and safe boundaries.
lessons.why_this_matters: Even simple hand tools can injure users if damaged or misused.

content_sections.heading: Inspect before use
paragraphs: Look for cracked handles, loose heads, damaged cutting edges, and other defects. Do not use or sell a tool as safe when damage is suspected.

content_sections.heading: Use tools as intended
paragraphs: Wear protective equipment specified by the tool and task. Keep cutting edges away from the body. Secure workpieces when appropriate. Follow manufacturer instructions.

content_sections.heading: Know what not to advise
paragraphs: Do not suggest using ordinary hand tools on live electrical parts. Do not improvise a tool as a lever or striking device beyond its intended use.

lessons.hardware_store_example: A customer asks if a regular screwdriver can be used on an energized outlet. You do not advise working live. You direct them to a qualified electrician and appropriate safety guidance.
what_to_say_or_do: Refer to the manufacturer safety instructions.
Stop when a task involves electrical or other serious hazards.
common_mistakes: Treating all screwdrivers as safe for electrical work.
lessons.when_to_ask_for_help: Refer electrical, gas, structural, and other high-risk tasks to qualified professionals.

supporting_materials.purpose: Illustrate the correct selection or safe tool-handling decision
supporting_materials.accessibility: Provide descriptive alt text naming the visible components. Do not use imagery as the only teaching source.

key_takeaways: Look for cracked handles, loose heads, damaged cutting edges, and other defects.
Refer electrical, gas, structural, and other high-risk tasks to qualified professionals.

unscored_practice.question: Before recommending a product, what would you check in this situation? A customer asks if a regular screwdriver can be used on an energized outlet. You do not advise working live. You direct them to a qualified electrician and appropriate safety guidance.
unscored_practice.answer: Check tool condition. Explain the intended use.
unscored_practice.explanation: Even simple hand tools can injure users if damaged or misused. Refer electrical, gas, structural, and other high-risk tasks to qualified professionals.

lessons.title: Care for and Store Hand Tools
lessons.objective: Describe basic inspection, cleaning, and storage.
lessons.why_this_matters: Well-kept tools are easier to find and less likely to fail unexpectedly.

content_sections.heading: Clean and dry
paragraphs: Remove ordinary dirt after use using manufacturer-approved methods. Dry tools before storage when appropriate. Follow instructions for rust prevention.

content_sections.heading: Protect edges and moving parts
paragraphs: Store sharp tools with guards when provided. Keep tools organized to prevent accidental contact and damage. Do not attempt repairs outside approved procedures.

content_sections.heading: Know replacement signs
paragraphs: Damaged handles, cracked sockets, or badly worn drivers may need replacement. Manufacturer guidance determines whether repair is allowed.

lessons.hardware_store_example: A customer asks how to store hand tools in a damp shed. You suggest a dry, organized location and checking the tool maker’s care guidance for rust prevention.
what_to_say_or_do: Refer damaged tools to appropriate service guidance.
common_mistakes: Leaving tools wet in a closed container.
Continuing to use a cracked tool.
lessons.when_to_ask_for_help: Ask a supervisor or manufacturer service contact about uncertain repairs or warranty questions.

supporting_materials.accessibility: Provide descriptive alt text naming the visible components. Do not use imagery as the only teaching source.

key_takeaways: Remove ordinary dirt after use using manufacturer-approved methods.

unscored_practice.question: Before recommending a product, what would you check in this situation? A customer asks how to store hand tools in a damp shed. You suggest a dry, organized location and checking the tool maker’s care guidance for rust prevention.
unscored_practice.answer: Recommend a dry storage space. Keep sharp edges protected.
